newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Consortium makes final bid for ZCCM mine.
newsitem.headline: Consortium makes final bid for ZCCM mine.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) said on Thursday it had received a final bid from the Kafue consortium for the purchase of the Nchanga-Nkana mining package.
"A final bid has been received from the Kafue consortium for the Nchanga-Nkana package and it is being evaluated," a ZCCM official told Reuters.
The Kafue consortium comprises Avmin, Noranda Mines, Phelps Dodge Corp and the Commonwealth Development Corporation.
"The negotiations for the Nchange-Nkana package are being conducted under the principle of willing seller and willing buyer.

"Although time is of the essence, the main objective of the negotiations is to achieve an equitable deal in which the interests of all the stakeholders are met in a balanced manner," the official said.
The Nchanga-Nkana package comprises five underground mines, one open pit mine, concentrator facilities, a tailings leach plant and a cobalt plant.
Meanwhile, Canada's First Quantum Minerals Ltd intends to appeal against last month's sale of ZCCM's Luanshya-Baluba package to Binani Industries, the official said.
"It is true that First Quantum intends to appeal against the decision over the package. We respect that intention as First Quantum's prerogative," the official said.
"However, we have not received official notification from First Quantumm of any intention to appeal."

The official dismissed reports that the Luanshya-Baluba package was awarded to Binani because cash-strapped ZCCM needed funds and Binani was willing to complete the sales negotiations before other bidders.

"The Binani group was chosen as the successful bidder because of the superior cash consideration plans for downstream projects and employment security at the time of the change of ownership," the official said.
"The award of the package to Binani is subject to contract, and finalisation of transaction agreements is expected by the end of the third quarter of 1997."
